Suppose we have a design matrix $$X$$ and observed response vector $$Y$$ that we assume are generated from some true linear model. Specifically, we assume
$$Y_i=f_{	heta**{*}}(X_i)+\epsilon_i$$
where
• $$X_i$$ represents the ith row of our design matrix, and $$Y_i$$ represents the ith true response value
• $$f_{	heta**{*}}(x)$$ represents the underlying true linear model, parametrized by $$	heta**{*}$$
• Each $$\epsilon_i$$ is a random variable with $$E[\epsilon_i]=0$$ and $$Var[\epsilon_i]=\sigma**{2}$$
We want to use a linear model $$\hat{Y}=X{	heta}$$ to fit our data.
Assume that $$X$$ and $$Y$$ refer to our entire dataset. After performing a train-test split, we use squared loss and $$L_2$$ regularization with a positive regularization hyperparameter $$\lambda$$ (i.e. ridge regression) to determine our parameter estimate $$\hat{	heta}$$ using just our training data.
For each of following questions, select all options that are true.
